Разнообразная двойная компиляция

Вы узнаете

Что доказывает совпадение, когда компилятор пересобран тремя путями и сравнен с собственным текстом.

Разнообразная двойная компиляция пересобирает компилятор другим путём и сравнивает результат с текстом компилятора. Здесь текст — вывод t27core.t27, а путей 3: gen-c и затем cc, t27b и эталон на Zig. ddc_verdict говорит «не может запуститься», когда собрано меньше 2 путей, «ошибка компиляции», когда вторая стадия собранного пути отличается, и «согласие», когда всё совпало: только бэкендов, пока все пути делят один фронтенд. Прогон со всеми 3 собранными путями, выявивший задачу 6292, нашёл дефект, который был у пути Zig и которого не было у двух других. Одна лишь неподвижная точка самосборки, путь A, его бы пропустила.

Попробовать

Начните с прогона на 0fbd183ba и сделайте так, чтобы путь Zig отличался. Потом верните его и снимите отметку общего фронтенда.

Открыть интерактивный урок →

Build the compiler again by three routes and compare each result with the compiler text itself. Set which routes were built and which matched, and see what the check can and cannot prove.

specs/compiler/theory/toolchain.t27

// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
; specs/compiler/theory/toolchain.t27 -- the toolchain theorems: what each check of t27c and t27b certifies
; (gHashTag/t27 epic #6488, Refs #6063, Refs #5980). ASCII only (L3).

; What a theorem is in this file. Each theorem is stated in prose, with the primary source it comes
; from, and is then checked on a small FINITE MODEL by the tests below. A finite-model check is not a
; proof of the general statement; it shows the statement holds on every case the model enumerates and
; that the test can fail (each section has a negative control that is asserted to disagree). The
; tests call functions, so every assert runs at run time: t27b counts them, and none of these tests
; is a vacuous pass (theorem T730 below says why that matters).

; Numbering. The theorems continue the project register docs/theory/IGLA-FORMAL-RESULTS.md, whose last
; entry on origin/master 6a2ad2352 is T727. This file uses T728..T734; the assembler round trip
; (specs/compiler/theory/isa_round_trip.t27) uses T735..T736; the compiler sieve
; (specs/compiler/theory/sieve.t27) starts at T737. Map to the working names of the research note:
; T1 = T728, T2 = T729, T3 = T730, T4 = T731, T5 = T735, T6 = T732, T7 = T733, ladder = T734.

; The verdict codes are the ones specs/tri/t27b/steward.t27 defines (PASS = 0, PASS_VACUOUS = 1,
; BLOCKED = 2, FRONTEND = 3, CODEGEN = 4, FAIL = 5, MISMATCH = 6); the ratchet theorem calls the
; steward's own cap rules through `use`, so it checks the rule that runs, not a copy of it.

; phi^2 + 1/phi^2 = 3 | TRINITY

module CompilerTheoryToolchain;

use tri::t27b::steward;

pub const V_PASS : u8 = 0;
pub const V_PASS_VACUOUS : u8 = 1;
pub const V_BLOCKED : u8 = 2;
pub const V_FAIL : u8 = 5;
pub const V_MISMATCH : u8 = 6;

; ==================================================================================================
; T728 (T1) -- what "t27b passes with runtime checks" certifies.
; Source: X. Leroy, "Formal verification of a realistic compiler", CACM 52(7):107-115, 2009: if the
; source program S does not go wrong, every observable behaviour of the compiled program C is an
; acceptable behaviour of S (for a deterministic language: proved forward, by induction on S's run). Translation validation (Pnueli, Siegel, Singerman, TACAS 1998; Necula,
; PLDI 2000, which validates GCC pass by pass) checks that property for ONE translation instead of for the compiler.
; Statement. A t27 test is a closed program: no input. If the native code of one test runs to the
; end and executes k > 0 runtime asserts, all true, and the reference path passes the same test,
; then for that one program the compiled behaviour and the reference behaviour agree on every
; executed assert. That is translation validation of one execution, not of the compiler: it says
; nothing about another program, and it is only as strong as the asserts (k = 0 certifies nothing,
; T730). A t27b pass where the reference does not pass is evidence of a run, not of preservation.
; Lab, master 682564f48 (t27b-lab latest.json, 2026-10-05T15:01Z): 380 such passes, 0 t27b passes
; where the reference does not pass.
; ==================================================================================================

pub const EV_NONE : u8 = 0;
pub const EV_RUN_ONLY : u8 = 1;
pub const EV_AGREES : u8 = 2;

pub fn evidence(reference: u8, native: u8, asserts: u32) -> u8 {
    if (native != V_PASS) { return EV_NONE; }
    if (asserts == 0) { return EV_NONE; }
    if (reference != V_PASS) { return EV_RUN_ONLY; }
    return EV_AGREES;
}

test t728_only_a_checked_agreeing_pass_is_evidence_of_preservation {
    assert evidence(V_PASS, V_PASS, 3) == EV_AGREES;
    assert evidence(V_FAIL, V_PASS, 3) == EV_RUN_ONLY;
    assert evidence(V_BLOCKED, V_PASS, 1) == EV_RUN_ONLY;
    assert evidence(V_PASS, V_PASS, 0) == EV_NONE;
    assert evidence(V_PASS, V_PASS_VACUOUS, 0) == EV_NONE;
    assert evidence(V_PASS, V_FAIL, 9) == EV_NONE;
    assert evidence(V_PASS, V_MISMATCH, 9) == EV_NONE;
}

test t728_evidence_never_exceeds_agreement_over_every_verdict_pair {
    var r : u8 = 0;
    var bad : u32 = 0;
    var agrees : u32 = 0;
    while (r < 7) {
        var n : u8 = 0;
        while (n < 7) {
            var k : u32 = 0;
            while (k < 3) {
                var e : u8 = evidence(r, n, k);
                if (e == EV_AGREES) {
                    agrees = agrees + 1;
                    if (r != V_PASS) { bad = bad + 1; }
                    if (n != V_PASS) { bad = bad + 1; }
                    if (k == 0) { bad = bad + 1; }
                }
                k = k + 1;
            }
            n = n + 1;
        }
        r = r + 1;
    }
    assert bad == 0;
    assert agrees == 2;
}

; ==================================================================================================
; T729 (T2) -- a differential oracle is sound for disagreement and blind to common mode.
; Sources: W. M. McKeeman, "Differential Testing for Software", Digital Technical Journal 10(1),
; 100-107, 1998 (bibliographic record verified; the paper text was not opened, so its wording is
; UNVERIFIED). X. Yang, Y. Chen, E. Eide, J. Regehr, "Finding and Understanding Bugs in C
; Compilers", PLDI 2011, DOI 10.1145/1993498.1993532 (Csmith: more than 325 previously unknown bugs,
; found by comparing compilers on generated programs). D. A. Wheeler, ACSAC 2005, compiles with a
; SECOND, trusted compiler for the reason part (b) states: a shared defect is invisible.
; Model. A compilation path is a set of stages (bit mask). A defect is a set of defective stages. A
; defect changes the output of every path that contains it; two paths disagree exactly when the
; defect touches a stage in one path and not the other (the symmetric difference).
; Statement. (a) Soundness: disagreement implies a defect in an unshared stage. (b) Common mode: a
; defect confined to stages both paths share is never seen; the blind spot is 2^shared - 1 non-empty
; defect sets over the stages of the pair.
; t27b today (cli/t27b/src/lib.rs mounts bootstrap/src/compiler.rs; front.rs: "exactly the t27c
; path"): the JIT is checked against eval.rs over the SAME IR from lower.rs, so a lowering defect
; makes both sides agree (#6441). Against the reference (t27c gen-zig + zig test) the shared stages
; are parse and typecheck. An independent front end (t27core's own lexer and parser, #5980) is the
; only pair in the model with nothing shared.
; ==================================================================================================

pub const ST_PARSE : u32 = 1;
pub const ST_TYPECHECK : u32 = 2;
pub const ST_LOWER : u32 = 4;
pub const ST_A64 : u32 = 8;
pub const ST_EVAL : u32 = 16;
pub const ST_GENZIG : u32 = 32;
pub const ST_ZIG : u32 = 64;
pub const ST_CORE_FRONT : u32 = 128;
pub const ST_ALL : u32 = 255;

pub const PAIR_JIT_INTERP : u8 = 0;
pub const PAIR_T27B_REFERENCE : u8 = 1;
pub const PAIR_T27B_CORE_FRONT : u8 = 2;

pub fn path_a(pair: u8) -> u32 {
    if (pair == PAIR_T27B_CORE_FRONT) { return ST_CORE_FRONT | ST_LOWER | ST_A64; }
    return ST_PARSE | ST_TYPECHECK | ST_LOWER | ST_A64;
}

pub fn path_b(pair: u8) -> u32 {
    if (pair == PAIR_JIT_INTERP) { return ST_PARSE | ST_TYPECHECK | ST_LOWER | ST_EVAL; }
    return ST_PARSE | ST_TYPECHECK | ST_GENZIG | ST_ZIG;
}

pub fn shared(pair: u8) -> u32 {
    return path_a(pair) & path_b(pair);
}

pub fn disagree(pair: u8, defect: u32) -> bool {
    return (defect & (path_a(pair) ^ path_b(pair))) != 0;
}

pub fn touches(pair: u8, defect: u32) -> bool {
    return (defect & (path_a(pair) | path_b(pair))) != 0;
}

; The number of non-empty defect sets within the pair's own stages that the pair cannot see.
pub fn blind_spot(pair: u8) -> u32 {
    var d : u32 = 1;
    var blind : u32 = 0;
    var outside : u32 = ST_ALL ^ (path_a(pair) | path_b(pair));
    while (d <= ST_ALL) {
        if ((d & outside) != 0) {
            d = d + 1;
            continue;
        }
        if (touches(pair, d)) {
            if (disagree(pair, d) == false) { blind = blind + 1; }
        }
        d = d + 1;
    }
    return blind;
}

test t729_disagreement_is_sound {
    var pair : u8 = 0;
    var unsound : u32 = 0;
    while (pair < 3) {
        var d : u32 = 0;
        while (d <= ST_ALL) {
            if (disagree(pair, d)) {
                if ((d & (path_a(pair) ^ path_b(pair))) == 0) { unsound = unsound + 1; }
                if (d == 0) { unsound = unsound + 1; }
            }
            d = d + 1;
        }
        pair = pair + 1;
    }
    assert unsound == 0;
}

test t729_the_blind_spot_is_the_shared_stages {
    assert shared(PAIR_JIT_INTERP) == (ST_PARSE | ST_TYPECHECK | ST_LOWER);
    assert shared(PAIR_T27B_REFERENCE) == (ST_PARSE | ST_TYPECHECK);
    assert shared(PAIR_T27B_CORE_FRONT) == 0;
    assert blind_spot(PAIR_JIT_INTERP) == 7;
    assert blind_spot(PAIR_T27B_REFERENCE) == 3;
    assert blind_spot(PAIR_T27B_CORE_FRONT) == 0;
}

test t729_a_lowering_defect_is_invisible_to_jit_versus_interpreter {
    assert disagree(PAIR_JIT_INTERP, ST_LOWER) == false;
    assert disagree(PAIR_T27B_REFERENCE, ST_LOWER);
    assert disagree(PAIR_JIT_INTERP, ST_A64);
    assert disagree(PAIR_T27B_REFERENCE, ST_PARSE) == false;
    assert disagree(PAIR_T27B_CORE_FRONT, ST_PARSE);
}

; ==================================================================================================
; T730 (T3) -- a pass with zero executed asserts certifies nothing.
; Sources: I. Beer, S. Ben-David, C. Eisner, Y. Rodeh, "Efficient Detection of Vacuity in ACTL
; Formulas", CAV 1997 (a property can hold for a reason unrelated to the design: vacuously). The
; t27b form: cli/t27b/tests/vacuous.rs and the `pass_vacuous` verdict (#6115).
; Model. The trivial backend compiles every test to "return": it executes no assert. It passes a
; test exactly when the test executes no assert.
; Statement. A pass certifies something only when the trivial backend would fail the same test, so
; coverage counts checked passes only. Lab, master 682564f48: 380 checked passes and 281 vacuous
; passes among 723 reference passes; counting the vacuous ones inflates 525 per mille to 914.
; ==================================================================================================

pub const LAB_REFERENCE_PASS : u32 = 723;
pub const LAB_T27B_CHECKED_PASS : u32 = 380;
pub const LAB_T27B_VACUOUS_PASS : u32 = 281;

pub fn trivial_backend_passes(asserts: u32) -> bool {
    return asserts == 0;
}

pub fn certifies(verdict: u8, asserts: u32) -> bool {
    if (verdict != V_PASS) { return false; }
    return trivial_backend_passes(asserts) == false;
}

pub fn per_mille(part: u32, whole: u32) -> u32 {
    if (whole == 0) { return 0; }
    return (part * 1000) / whole;
}

test t730_a_certifying_pass_is_one_the_trivial_backend_fails {
    var v : u8 = 0;
    var bad : u32 = 0;
    while (v < 7) {
        var k : u32 = 0;
        while (k < 4) {
            if (certifies(v, k)) {
                if (trivial_backend_passes(k)) { bad = bad + 1; }
            }
            k = k + 1;
        }
        v = v + 1;
    }
    assert bad == 0;
    assert certifies(V_PASS, 1);
    assert certifies(V_PASS, 0) == false;
    assert certifies(V_PASS_VACUOUS, 0) == false;
}

test t730_the_lab_coverage_counts_checked_passes_only {
    assert per_mille(LAB_T27B_CHECKED_PASS, LAB_REFERENCE_PASS) == 525;
    assert per_mille(LAB_T27B_CHECKED_PASS + LAB_T27B_VACUOUS_PASS, LAB_REFERENCE_PASS) == 914;
}

; ==================================================================================================
; T731 (T4) -- the expectation ledger's cap only moves down.
; Source: the ratchet of docs/reports/t27b_expectations.json, decided by specs/tri/t27b/steward.t27
; (`cap_rises`, `over_cap`). Statement. If every bless is refused when `cap_rises`, the cap sequence
; is non-increasing, and every run the ratchet accepts has at most the first cap of non-passes.
; Model: 400 runs whose non-pass counts come from a linear congruential sequence in 0..99.
; Negative control: a bless that always takes the run's count raises the cap on the same sequence.
; ==================================================================================================

pub fn next_cap(old_cap: u32, not_pass: u32) -> u32 {
    if (cap_rises(not_pass, old_cap, true)) { return old_cap; }
    return not_pass;
}

pub fn lcg(x: u32) -> u32 {
    return (x * 1103 + 12345) % 65536;
}

test t731_the_cap_never_rises_and_bounds_every_accepted_run {
    var seed : u32 = 27;
    var cap : u32 = 60;
    var first : u32 = 60;
    var rises : u32 = 0;
    var naive : u32 = 60;
    var naive_rises : u32 = 0;
    var accepted_over_first : u32 = 0;
    var accepted : u32 = 0;
    var i : u32 = 0;
    while (i < 400) {
        seed = lcg(seed);
        var not_pass : u32 = seed % 100;
        if (over_cap(not_pass, cap, true) == false) {
            accepted = accepted + 1;
            if (not_pass > first) { accepted_over_first = accepted_over_first + 1; }
        }
        var c : u32 = next_cap(cap, not_pass);
        if (c > cap) { rises = rises + 1; }
        cap = c;
        if (not_pass > naive) { naive_rises = naive_rises + 1; }
        naive = not_pass;
        i = i + 1;
    }
    assert rises == 0;
    assert accepted_over_first == 0;
    assert accepted > 0;
    assert naive_rises > 0;
}

; ==================================================================================================
; T732 (T6) -- Diverse Double-Compiling on t27core.
; Sources: K. Thompson, "Reflections on Trusting Trust", CACM 27(8), 1984 (a compiler binary can
; carry a trojan that re-inserts itself when it compiles the compiler, invisible in every source).
; D. A. Wheeler, "Countering Trusting Trust through Diverse Double-Compiling", ACSAC 2005, and
; PhD dissertation, George Mason University, 2009: compile the compiler's source with an
; independent trusted compiler (stage 1), compile the source again with the result (stage 2), and
; compare stage 2 bit for bit with the compiler under test.
; Statement for t27. Let S = specs/compiler/core/t27core.t27 (deterministic) and E = t27c gen-c(S),
; the C text S must reproduce byte for byte (its fixpoint, gated in bootstrap/tests/core_selfhost.rs).
; A route builds a stage-1 core from S with one back end; running that core on S is its stage 2.
; Route A builds with t27c gen-c + cc, route B with t27b (AArch64), route C with the t27c Zig
; reference (gen-zig + zig). If a route's back end is correct for S, its stage 2 equals E. A route
; whose stage 2 differs from E proves that its back end (or gen-c, which made E) miscompiles S.
; Equality on every route proves nothing about a defect all routes share (T729): t27b mounts
; bootstrap/src/compiler.rs's parser and type checker by #[path], and gen-c and gen-zig run behind
; the same parser, so the diversity is in the back ends only. This is weaker than Wheeler's
; independence until the shared front end is removed (pair PAIR_T27B_CORE_FRONT of T729).
; What now holds (PR #6825, Closes #6508, commit 0fbd183ba). The check runs. The harness is
; specs/compiler/core/t27core_ddc.t27: it imports S's functions through `use`, carries S and E as
; data pinned by sha256, runs S's `compile` on S, compares with E, and requires one flipped byte to
; be found (negative control). t27core.t27 itself passes 8/8 tests on the Zig reference and 8/8 on
; t27b (`t27b test --check`, 19 runtime asserts). Stage 2 equals E on all three routes: route A as
; the core_selfhost fixpoint (run on the t27c lab, log copied to
; https://t27b-lab-production.up.railway.app/ddc6508/0fbd183ba-core_selfhost.out), route B as a t27b PASS with 7 runtime asserts and JIT ==
; interpreter, route C as a reference PASS; `t27b corpus specs/compiler/core --reference` reports
; 0 files, 0 tests disagreeing. Lab records:
;   https://t27b-lab-production.up.railway.app/ddc6508/0fbd183ba.out
;   https://t27c-lab-production.up.railway.app/runs/0fbd183bae84d02f07a36aac98aed30e6b5992c6.json
; Before #6825 it could not run: t27b was BLOCKED on t27core.t27 ("StmtAssign(reference
; redeclares)", "ExprArrayLiteral(repeat)") and S needed `as usize` indexes before Zig built it.
; The run found two defects. #6292: gen-zig hoisted a repeated `p + 1` above a write to `p`, so the
; first route C stage 2 differed from E while A and B matched it (S now steps with `advance()`; the
; compiler bug stays open). #6802: a hex literal whose digits end in f16, f32 or f64 loses those
; digits in the shared front end (the harness data is decimal because of it). Two more limits from
; the harness header: the comparison runs inside each stage-1 program, so the flipped-byte control
; rules out a no-op comparison but not a targeted trojan; and S and E are pinned, so after S
; changes the data must be regenerated.
; Model, part 1: the verdict rule over routes (bit mask). Fewer than two built routes: the check
; cannot run. A built route whose stage 2 is not E: a miscompile is proven. All built routes equal:
; agreement, of back ends only while the front end is shared (taken from T729's shared(), not
; restated). Negative control: the fixpoint alone (route A) passes the first route C run that
; DDC flags.
; Model, part 2 (Thompson): compilers are binaries 0..3: 0 honest, 1 Thompson trojan (miscompiles
; the login source and re-inserts itself into the compiler source), 2 a plain miscompiler of the
; compiler source, 3 the output of compiling the honest compiler source with a correct compiler
; (equals 0 by construction).
; ==================================================================================================

pub const SRC_COMPILER : u32 = 0;
pub const SRC_LOGIN : u32 = 1;
pub const BIN_HONEST : u32 = 0;
pub const BIN_TROJAN : u32 = 1;
pub const BIN_MISCOMPILER : u32 = 2;
pub const BIN_LOGIN_OK : u32 = 10;
pub const BIN_LOGIN_BACKDOOR : u32 = 11;

pub fn compile_with(bin: u32, src: u32) -> u32 {
    if (src == SRC_LOGIN) {
        if (bin == BIN_TROJAN) { return BIN_LOGIN_BACKDOOR; }
        return BIN_LOGIN_OK;
    }
    if (bin == BIN_TROJAN) { return BIN_TROJAN; }
    if (bin == BIN_MISCOMPILER) { return BIN_MISCOMPILER; }
    return BIN_HONEST;
}

pub fn stage2(trusted: u32) -> u32 {
    var stage1 : u32 = compile_with(trusted, SRC_COMPILER);
    return compile_with(stage1, SRC_COMPILER);
}

pub fn ddc_flags(trusted: u32, under_test: u32) -> bool {
    return stage2(trusted) != under_test;
}

test t732_ddc_catches_the_trojan_with_an_independent_compiler {
    assert ddc_flags(BIN_HONEST, BIN_TROJAN);
    assert ddc_flags(BIN_HONEST, BIN_MISCOMPILER);
    assert ddc_flags(BIN_HONEST, BIN_HONEST) == false;
    assert compile_with(BIN_TROJAN, SRC_LOGIN) == BIN_LOGIN_BACKDOOR;
}

test t732_a_shared_trojan_is_common_mode {
    assert ddc_flags(BIN_TROJAN, BIN_TROJAN) == false;
    assert stage2(BIN_TROJAN) == BIN_TROJAN;
}

pub const ROUTE_GENC_CC : u32 = 1;
pub const ROUTE_T27B : u32 = 2;
pub const ROUTE_ZIG : u32 = 4;
pub const ROUTE_ALL : u32 = 7;

pub const DDC_CANNOT_RUN : u8 = 0;
pub const DDC_MISCOMPILE : u8 = 1;
pub const DDC_AGREE_BACK_ENDS : u8 = 2;
pub const DDC_AGREE_INDEPENDENT : u8 = 3;

; The recorded runs. `built`: routes whose stage-1 core was built and ran on S. `equal`: routes whose
; stage 2 was byte-identical to E.
; Before #6825 (master 5bad20521): only route A built (t27b BLOCKED, Zig needed `as usize`).
pub const RUN_BEFORE_BUILT : u32 = 1;
pub const RUN_BEFORE_EQUAL : u32 = 1;
; First run with all three routes (#6292): the Zig-built core differed from E.
pub const RUN_FIRST_ZIG_BUILT : u32 = 7;
pub const RUN_FIRST_ZIG_EQUAL : u32 = 3;
; Commit 0fbd183ba (PR #6825): all three built, all three equal to E.
pub const RUN_0FBD183BA_BUILT : u32 = 7;
pub const RUN_0FBD183BA_EQUAL : u32 = 7;

pub fn route_count(mask: u32) -> u32 {
    var m : u32 = mask;
    var n : u32 = 0;
    while (m > 0) {
        if ((m & 1) != 0) { n = n + 1; }
        m = m / 2;
    }
    return n;
}

pub fn ddc_verdict(built: u32, equal: u32, front_shared: bool) -> u8 {
    if (route_count(built & ROUTE_ALL) < 2) { return DDC_CANNOT_RUN; }
    if ((built & equal) != built) { return DDC_MISCOMPILE; }
    if (front_shared) { return DDC_AGREE_BACK_ENDS; }
    return DDC_AGREE_INDEPENDENT;
}

; The negative control: the self-host fixpoint alone (route A), with no second route.
pub fn fixpoint_only_passes(equal: u32) -> bool {
    return (equal & ROUTE_GENC_CC) != 0;
}

test t732_the_recorded_runs_get_the_verdict_the_text_states {
    var shared_front : bool = shared(PAIR_T27B_REFERENCE) != 0;
    assert shared_front;
    assert ddc_verdict(RUN_BEFORE_BUILT, RUN_BEFORE_EQUAL, shared_front) == DDC_CANNOT_RUN;
    assert ddc_verdict(RUN_FIRST_ZIG_BUILT, RUN_FIRST_ZIG_EQUAL, shared_front) == DDC_MISCOMPILE;
    assert ddc_verdict(RUN_0FBD183BA_BUILT, RUN_0FBD183BA_EQUAL, shared_front) == DDC_AGREE_BACK_ENDS;
    var own_front : bool = shared(PAIR_T27B_CORE_FRONT) != 0;
    assert ddc_verdict(RUN_0FBD183BA_BUILT, RUN_0FBD183BA_EQUAL, own_front) == DDC_AGREE_INDEPENDENT;
}

test t732_the_fixpoint_alone_misses_what_ddc_flags {
    assert fixpoint_only_passes(RUN_FIRST_ZIG_EQUAL);
    assert ddc_verdict(RUN_FIRST_ZIG_BUILT, RUN_FIRST_ZIG_EQUAL, true) == DDC_MISCOMPILE;
}

test t732_agreement_needs_two_routes_and_every_built_route_equal {
    var built : u32 = 0;
    var bad : u32 = 0;
    var back_ends : u32 = 0;
    var independent : u32 = 0;
    while (built <= ROUTE_ALL) {
        var equal : u32 = 0;
        while (equal <= ROUTE_ALL) {
            var sh : u32 = 0;
            while (sh < 2) {
                var v : u8 = ddc_verdict(built, equal, sh == 1);
                if (v == DDC_AGREE_BACK_ENDS) {
                    back_ends = back_ends + 1;
                    if (sh == 0) { bad = bad + 1; }
                }
                if (v == DDC_AGREE_INDEPENDENT) {
                    independent = independent + 1;
                    if (sh == 1) { bad = bad + 1; }
                }
                if (v >= DDC_AGREE_BACK_ENDS) {
                    if (route_count(built) < 2) { bad = bad + 1; }
                    if ((built & equal) != built) { bad = bad + 1; }
                }
                sh = sh + 1;
            }
            equal = equal + 1;
        }
        built = built + 1;
    }
    assert bad == 0;
    assert back_ends == 7;
    assert independent == 7;
}

; ==================================================================================================
; T733 (T7) -- JIT == interpreter is the first Futamura projection's correctness equation.
; Source: Y. Futamura, "Partial Evaluation of Computation Process -- An Approach to a
; Compiler-Compiler", Higher-Order and Symbolic Computation 12(4):381-391, 1999 (reprint of the 1971
; paper in Systems, Computers, Controls 2(5), which was not opened: UNVERIFIED), abstract: a compiler
; is obtained from an interpreter by partial evaluation. First projection, in its standard reading
; (the exact wording behind the paywall was not opened: UNVERIFIED): specialising an interpreter to
; a fixed program yields a compiled program with run(mix(interp, p), x) == interp(p, x) for all x.
; Statement for t27. t27b's JIT is a compiler, not a specialiser, but the check t27b runs per test
; (`t27b test --check`: every value and trap site of the JIT must be the one eval.rs computes) is
; exactly this equation with eval.rs as the interpreter. Its strength is bounded by T729: both read
; the IR of lower.rs, so the equation certifies codegen against the IR, not the IR against t27.
; Model. A program is a base-4 digit string (digit 0 ends it): 1 is x+1, 2 is 2x, 3 is x-1, all
; modulo the prime 1009. The interpreter runs the digits. The compiler specialises the interpreter
; to the program: it folds the digits into the affine pair (a, b) with result a*x + b. The theorem
; checks every one of the 1024 programs of up to five digits at 12 inputs. Negative control: a
; folder that forgets to double the constant disagrees on some program.
; ==================================================================================================

pub const FUT_P : u32 = 1009;

pub fn op_apply(op: u32, x: u32) -> u32 {
    if (op == 1) { return (x + 1) % FUT_P; }
    if (op == 2) { return (x * 2) % FUT_P; }
    if (op == 3) { return (x + FUT_P - 1) % FUT_P; }
    return x;
}

pub fn interp(prog: u32, x: u32) -> u32 {
    var p : u32 = prog;
    var v : u32 = x % FUT_P;
    while (p > 0) {
        var op : u32 = p % 4;
        if (op == 0) { return v; }
        v = op_apply(op, v);
        p = p / 4;
    }
    return v;
}

; mix(interp, prog): the slope of the specialised program.
pub fn fold_a(prog: u32) -> u32 {
    var p : u32 = prog;
    var a : u32 = 1;
    while (p > 0) {
        var op : u32 = p % 4;
        if (op == 0) { return a; }
        if (op == 2) { a = (a * 2) % FUT_P; }
        p = p / 4;
    }
    return a;
}

; mix(interp, prog): the constant of the specialised program. `careless` forgets that doubling
; also doubles the constant (2(ax + b) = 2ax + 2b): the negative control.
pub fn fold_b(prog: u32, careless: bool) -> u32 {
    var p : u32 = prog;
    var b : u32 = 0;
    while (p > 0) {
        var op : u32 = p % 4;
        if (op == 0) { return b; }
        if (op == 1) { b = (b + 1) % FUT_P; }
        if (op == 2) {
            if (careless == false) { b = (b * 2) % FUT_P; }
        }
        if (op == 3) { b = (b + FUT_P - 1) % FUT_P; }
        p = p / 4;
    }
    return b;
}

pub fn run_compiled(a: u32, b: u32, x: u32) -> u32 {
    return ((a * (x % FUT_P)) % FUT_P + b) % FUT_P;
}

pub fn futamura_disagreements(careless: bool) -> u32 {
    var prog : u32 = 0;
    var bad : u32 = 0;
    while (prog < 1024) {
        var a : u32 = fold_a(prog);
        var b : u32 = fold_b(prog, careless);
        var x : u32 = 0;
        while (x < 12) {
            var xi : u32 = x * 97;
            if (run_compiled(a, b, xi) != interp(prog, xi)) { bad = bad + 1; }
            x = x + 1;
        }
        prog = prog + 1;
    }
    return bad;
}

test t733_the_specialised_program_equals_the_interpreter_everywhere {
    assert futamura_disagreements(false) == 0;
}

test t733_the_check_can_fail {
    assert futamura_disagreements(true) > 0;
}

; ==================================================================================================
; T734 -- the ladder: t27a, t27b, t27c, and why backend correctness reduces to instruction selection.
; t27c = the compiler (bootstrap/src, gen-zig, gen-c, gen-rust, gen-verilog, gen-js, typecheck).
; t27b = the native backend (cli/t27b: front.rs, lower.rs, eval.rs, a64.rs, jit.rs, macho.rs).
; t27a = the assembler and disassembler, which does NOT exist as a tool. Its pieces exist:
; specs/isa/ternary_encoding.t27 (encode and field decoders of the TRI-27 word),
; specs/fpga/assembler.t27 (sections, relocations, symbols for the ternary core),
; specs/isa/registers.t27 (27 registers), and for AArch64 cli/t27b/src/a64.rs (an encoder with a
; disassembler, checked word for word against clang in cli/t27b/tests/encoder.rs).
; Statement. Let a backend be isel ; encode, where isel maps IR to instructions and encode maps an
; instruction to a word. If decode(encode(i)) = i for every well-formed instruction i (T735), then
; any wrong word the backend emits for a well-formed instruction is an isel defect: the encoding
; layer is ruled out, and backend correctness reduces to instruction selection (the reduction the
; SLED/NJMCT work of N. Ramsey and M. F. Fernandez, TOPLAS 19(3), 1997, makes by generating encoder
; and decoder from one specification; J. Dias and N. Ramsey, POPL 2010, then generate isel from
; declarative machine descriptions). T735 finds that the current TRI-27 encoding does NOT round-trip
; for DOT, BIND, BUNDLE2 (src2 lost), SACR (immediate lost) and BUNDLE3 (not writable by encode),
; so today the reduction holds for 42 of the 47 opcodes only.
; Model: a word is wrong when isel or encode is wrong. With a round-tripping encoder, the
; disassembled word names the isel output exactly, so blame is decidable.
; ==================================================================================================

pub const LAYER_ISEL : u8 = 1;
pub const LAYER_ENCODE : u8 = 2;

pub fn blame(isel_ok: bool, encode_round_trips: bool, word_ok: bool) -> u8 {
    if (word_ok) { return 0; }
    if (encode_round_trips) { return LAYER_ISEL; }
    if (isel_ok) { return LAYER_ENCODE; }
    return LAYER_ISEL | LAYER_ENCODE;
}

test t734_a_round_tripping_encoder_leaves_only_isel_to_blame {
    assert blame(false, true, false) == LAYER_ISEL;
    assert blame(true, false, false) == LAYER_ENCODE;
    assert blame(false, false, false) == (LAYER_ISEL | LAYER_ENCODE);
    assert blame(true, true, true) == 0;
}

; ==================================================================================================
; The letters. Which further t27<letter> tools are artifacts and which would be numerology.
; A tool letter is admitted only if the repository has an artifact for it AND a theorem that says
; what its check certifies. The agent of docs/agents/AGENTS_ALPHABET.md that owns it is named by
; DOMAIN, not by letter: the coincidence t27a/t27b/t27c = assembler/backend/compiler is an English
; mnemonic, and the agent letters A, B, C mean Architecture, Build and Compiler Core. So t27a belongs
; to agent I (ISA / Registers), t27b and t27c to agent C (Compiler Core).
;   admitted, artifact exists: t27c (C), t27b (C).
;   admitted, artifact partly exists and the theorem is T735/T736: t27a (I).
;   candidate, artifact exists as a spec only: a linker (specs/fpga/linker.t27 for the ternary core,
;     specs/compiler/linker.t27 for modules; cli/t27b/src/macho.rs writes relocatable objects).
;     Owner K or B. No theorem yet (it would be: link then disassemble equals the relocated
;     assembly). Not admitted until it has one.
;   candidate: a cycle simulator (specs/fpga/simulator.t27, agent K) and a formal checker
;     (specs/fpga/formal.t27, agent V). Same rule: no theorem, no letter.
;   refused: a debugger (no artifact), a "t27d".. "t27z" series filled to 27 (no artifact; that is
;     numerology, which docs/COMPETITIVE_ANALYSIS_SCIENTIFIC_FOUNDATIONS.md section 8.3 warns about).
; ==================================================================================================

pub const AGENT_C : u8 = 3;
pub const AGENT_I : u8 = 9;
pub const AGENT_K : u8 = 11;
pub const AGENT_V : u8 = 22;

pub const TOOL_A : u8 = 1;
pub const TOOL_B : u8 = 2;
pub const TOOL_C : u8 = 3;

pub fn owner_of_tool(tool: u8) -> u8 {
    if (tool == TOOL_A) { return AGENT_I; }
    if (tool == TOOL_B) { return AGENT_C; }
    if (tool == TOOL_C) { return AGENT_C; }
    return 0;
}

pub fn admitted(has_artifact: bool, has_theorem: bool) -> bool {
    if (has_artifact == false) { return false; }
    return has_theorem;
}

test t734_the_tool_letter_is_not_the_agent_letter {
    var tool : u8 = 1;
    var same : u32 = 0;
    while (tool <= 3) {
        if (owner_of_tool(tool) == tool) { same = same + 1; }
        tool = tool + 1;
    }
    assert same == 1;
    assert owner_of_tool(TOOL_A) == AGENT_I;
    assert admitted(true, true);
    assert admitted(true, false) == false;
    assert admitted(false, true) == false;
}

; ==================================================================================================
; How the 27 agents connect (proposal; the hive routing of PR #6430 is the transport and is not
; repeated here).
; 1. Ownership is a PARTITION of specs: every spec has exactly one owning agent (specs/OWNERS.md
;    gives it per subtree). Invariant: no spec has zero or two owners.
; 2. Edges are `use` imports between specs; the agent graph is the quotient of the import graph by
;    ownership. Agent G (Graph) holds its entry invariant: the graph is acyclic.
; 3. A contract on an edge is a conformance vector set (agent F, conformance/*.json), and a verdict
;    on the contract is agent V's. The chain is G (which edges exist) -> F (what crosses each edge)
;    -> V (did it hold).
; 4. The Queen (T) dispatches an issue to the owner of the paths in its Boundary: the partition makes
;    that a function, so two agents never hold the same path.
; Model. Six specs with owners, and the toolchain import graph t27c <- t27b, t27a <- t27b,
; isa <- t27a; a back edge t27a -> t27b is the negative control and must be found as a cycle.
; ==================================================================================================

pub const NODE_ISA : u32 = 0;
pub const NODE_T27A : u32 = 1;
pub const NODE_T27B : u32 = 2;
pub const NODE_T27C : u32 = 3;
pub const NODE_STEWARD : u32 = 4;
pub const NODE_THEORY : u32 = 5;
pub const NODES : u32 = 6;

; Owner bit mask of one node: exactly one bit is a partition.
pub fn owners(node: u32) -> u32 {
    if (node == NODE_ISA) { return 512; }
    if (node == NODE_T27A) { return 512; }
    if (node == NODE_T27B) { return 8; }
    if (node == NODE_T27C) { return 8; }
    if (node == NODE_STEWARD) { return 1048576; }
    return 8;
}

pub fn one_bit(m: u32) -> bool {
    if (m == 0) { return false; }
    return (m & (m - 1)) == 0;
}

; Import edges as a bit mask per node: bit j of uses(i) means node i uses node j.
pub fn uses(node: u32, back_edge: bool) -> u32 {
    if (node == NODE_T27A) {
        if (back_edge) { return 1 | 4; }
        return 1;
    }
    if (node == NODE_T27B) { return 2 | 8; }
    if (node == NODE_THEORY) { return 16; }
    return 0;
}

; Kahn's algorithm on the six-node graph: true when every node can be removed.
pub fn acyclic(back_edge: bool) -> bool {
    var removed : u32 = 0;
    var progress : bool = true;
    while (progress) {
        progress = false;
        var n : u32 = 0;
        while (n < NODES) {
            var bit : u32 = 1 << n;
            if ((removed & bit) == 0) {
                if ((uses(n, back_edge) & (removed ^ 63)) == 0) {
                    removed = removed | bit;
                    progress = true;
                }
            }
            n = n + 1;
        }
    }
    return removed == 63;
}

test agents_ownership_is_a_partition {
    var n : u32 = 0;
    var bad : u32 = 0;
    while (n < NODES) {
        if (one_bit(owners(n)) == false) { bad = bad + 1; }
        n = n + 1;
    }
    assert bad == 0;
    assert one_bit(512 | 8) == false;
    assert one_bit(0) == false;
}

test agents_the_toolchain_graph_is_acyclic_and_the_back_edge_is_caught {
    assert acyclic(false);
    assert acyclic(true) == false;
}

; ==================================================================================================
; The 3 x 3 x 3 cube, as a hypothesis only. Index the alphabet 0..26 (A..Z, then the 27th) and read
; it as (layer, role, phase) = (i / 9, (i / 3) % 3, i % 3). The layer coordinate IS the nona split of
; docs/README.md (A-I, J-R, S-27th): true by definition, so it predicts nothing. Role and phase have no
; measured consequence: the test the hypothesis would have to pass is that agents sharing a role
; coordinate share more import edges than agents that do not, measured on the real ownership
; quotient of the import graph. That measurement has not been made; until it is, the cube is a
; layout, not a finding.
; ==================================================================================================

pub fn cube_layer(i: u32) -> u32 { return i / 9; }
pub fn cube_role(i: u32) -> u32 { return (i / 3) % 3; }
pub fn cube_phase(i: u32) -> u32 { return i % 3; }

test cube_the_layer_is_the_nona_split_and_nothing_more {
    assert cube_layer(0) == 0;
    assert cube_layer(8) == 0;
    assert cube_layer(9) == 1;
    assert cube_layer(17) == 1;
    assert cube_layer(18) == 2;
    assert cube_layer(26) == 2;
    var i : u32 = 0;
    var cells : u32 = 0;
    while (i < 27) {
        cells = cells | (1 << (cube_layer(i) * 9 + cube_role(i) * 3 + cube_phase(i)));
        i = i + 1;
    }
    assert cells == 134217727;
}
